entries.proposition: In heterozygous Scn2a nonsense knock-in mice the authors report a higher prevalence and a greater incidence of epileptiform discharges than in wild-type mice (Fisher's exact P = 0.0455; Mann-Whitney P = 0.0025).
entries.snippet: Scn2aRX/+ mice had a higher prevalence and a greater incidence of epileptiform discharges than Scn2a+/+ mice (prevalence rate: Fisher’s exact test, *P = 0.0455, hourly incidence: Mann–Whitney test, U = 0, **P = 0.0025, Fig. 2b)

entries.proposition: Figure 2 read as an image: panel b prints prevalence 2/5 for wild type and 7/7 for the heterozygotes; the wild-type bar is near 0 and the heterozygous bar near 1 discharge per hour with one point near 4.3; panel d and e latency points shorter in the heterozygotes for sudden immobility and myoclonus (star), not for clonic or tonic-clonic convulsion.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2: prevalence 2/5 (+/+) vs 7/7 (RX/+); RX/+ bar about 1 SWD per hour, one point near 4.3; PTZ latency panels star for sudden immobility and myoclonus only.

entries.proposition: In Scn2aKO/+ mice two prolonged non-convulsive seizures were seen in 2 out of 6 animals recorded.
entries.snippet: ECoG monitoring further revealed two prolonged non-convulsive seizures with duration of 30–45 s in 2 out of 6 Scn2aKO/+ mice examined (Fig. 3b)

entries.proposition: In heterozygous Scn2a knockout mice, local field potential discharges were significantly raised in medial prefrontal cortex and caudate putamen (each P = 0.0286) and were not different from wild type in the ventroposterior thalamus (P > 0.9999).
entries.snippet: Mann–Whitney test, medial prefrontal cortex: U = 0, *P = 0.0286; visual cortex: U = 8, P > 0.9999; basolateral amygdala: U = 3, P = 0.2571; hippocampus CA1: U = 4, P = 0.4286; caudate putamen: U = 0, *P = 0.0286; ventroposterior thalamus: U = 7.5, P > 0.9999

entries.proposition: In mice with Scn2a deleted in dorsal telencephalic excitatory neurons, local field potential discharges were also significantly raised in the ventroposterior thalamus (U = 0, P = 0.0286), together with the somatosensory cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, basolateral amygdala and caudate putamen.
entries.snippet: Mann–Whitney test, ECoG, somatosensory cortex: U = 0, *P = 0.0286; LFP, medial prefrontal cortex: U = 0, *P = 0.0286; visual cortex: U = 6, P > 0.999; basolateral amygdala: U = 0, *P = 0.0268; hippocampus CA1: U = 4, P = 0.4286; caudate putamen: U = 0, *P = 0.0268; ventroposterior thalamus: U = 0, *P = 0.0286

entries.proposition: The authors report seizures about ten times more frequent in the excitatory-neuron deletion than in the knock-in heterozygotes (U = 2, P = 0.0088).
entries.snippet: Absence-like seizures appeared ~ 10 × more frequently in Scn2afl/+/Emx1-Cre than in Scn2aRX/+ mice (Mann–Whitney test, Scn2aRX/+ vs. Scn2afl/+/Emx1-Cre: U = 2, **P = 0.0088)

entries.proposition: The authors cite their earlier report that deletion of Cacna1a in cortical layer VI cells raised T-type current in thalamic relay neurons and caused absence epilepsy, and suggest impaired cortical excitatory input to thalamus may explain the ethosuximide-sensitive seizures in Scn2a-deficient mice (a suggestion, not tested here).
entries.snippet: Recently, we reported that a selective Cacna1a gene deletion in cortical layer VI pyramidal cells, which innervate thalamic relay neurons and reticular thalamic neurons, caused upregulation of T-type calcium current in thalamic relay neurons and resulted in absence epilepsy in mice59, suggesting that impaired cortical excitatory input to thalamic regions may cause rebound burst of thalamocortical relay neurons and leads to thalamocortical hyper-synchronous oscillations as may be the case for ethosuximide-sensitive absence-like seizures in Scn2a-deficient mice

entries.proposition: The authors offer, as an untested alternative, that removing Nav1.2 from excitatory neurons may shift excitation and inhibition toward inhibition, with hyperpolarization and low-threshold rebound firing through de-inactivation of T-type calcium currents.
entries.snippet: selective Nav1.2 elimination in excitatory neurons may shift an excitation/inhibition balance toward inhibition, which enhances hyperpolarization of neurons and low threshold rebound burst-firing via de-inactivation of T-type calcium currents, increasing the risk of SWD generation

entries.proposition: The authors state that the circuit basis of the absence-like seizures in the Scn2a-deficient mice requires further study.
entries.snippet: Thus, the circuit basis for the development of absence-like seizures in mice with Scn2a-deficiency requires further study.
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph on circuit mechanisms, last sentence
